title: Chart Type Selection Guide
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Follow a decision tree from what you want to show to the chart that fits your data, then practice on ten short data scenarios with immediate feedback.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to choose an appropriate chart type for a dataset by identifying the goal of the visualization and the structure of the data.
prerequisites: Line, scatter, bar, histogram, box, and pie charts

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Decision tree with worked examples, followed by scenario practice with immediate feedback
keyQuestions: What is the difference between showing a comparison and showing a composition?
Why does the number of categories change which bar chart to use?
When is a pie chart acceptable, and what should replace it when it is not?
commonMisconceptions: The chart type depends only on the data (the same data can need different charts for different questions).
Pie charts work for any number of categories (beyond about five slices the angles are too hard to compare).
A histogram is a bar chart (a histogram bins one numeric variable, while a bar chart compares separate categories).
3D effects make a chart clearer (perspective distorts the sizes the reader is supposed to compare).
assessmentOpportunities: Given four new descriptions of data and a question about each, students name the goal, the chart type, and the reason, and identify one chart that would be a poor choice for each and why.
